title: Heap gets corrupted after the name is saved. Tap the bug.
explain: strlen does not count the end byte '\0'. strcpy writes strlen + 1 bytes, so it writes one byte past the block. This corrupts the heap and often fails much later. Always allocate strlen(s) + 1 for a copy.

title: STM32 SPI master. spi_read_byte() hangs forever. Tap the bug.
explain: An SPI master makes the clock only when it sends a byte. Nothing is written to DR, so there is no clock and RXNE never becomes 1. To read, first write a dummy byte (for example 0xFF), then wait for RXNE. SPI is always a full-duplex swap.

title: The firmware resets every time max_sample() runs. Tap the bug.
explain: 0..=buf.len() includes buf.len(), but the last valid index is len - 1. On the last step buf[i] panics, and in firmware a panic usually means a reset. Use 0..buf.len(), or better, loop over the items with an iterator and no index.

pr.title: Stop SPI flash CS glitch at boot
pr.author: mia-dev
pr.body: The flash saw a short low pulse on CS at power-up. Now CS is set high before the pin becomes an output.

explain: Good change. The output data register is 0 after reset. If the pin becomes an output first, it drives low for a moment and the flash can see a start of a command. Writing the high level first means the pin goes high from its first output moment. Order matters in GPIO init.

pr.title: Tidy led_init: clock line at the end
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: I moved the RCC line below the GPIO lines, so all RCC code stays together.

explain: A peripheral without a clock ignores writes to its registers. Now MODER and BSRR are written while GPIOA has no clock, so the pin stays an input and the LED never works. Always enable the clock first, then configure the peripheral.

pr.title: Simplify wait_ready
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: The loop with the counter is ugly. A plain while loop is shorter and does the same.

explain: It is not the same. The old code gave up after 10 000 tries and reported Timeout. The new loop waits forever if the sensor is unplugged or broken, and the watchdog then resets the board in a loop. Every wait on hardware needs a limit and an error path.

title: Find the highest set bit. What does this print?
explain: x has 8 bits: 0001_0000. Three zeros are before the single 1, so leading_zeros is 3. Four zeros are after it, so trailing_zeros is 4. The bit index is 7 - leading_zeros = 4. Both methods are fast: they use one CPU instruction on many MCUs.

title: What does this print?
explain: A macro pastes its argument text, so i++ appears twice. The test i++ > 3 reads 5 and makes i 6. Then the chosen branch i++ runs again: it gives 6 and makes i 7. So r is 6 and i is 7. Never pass an expression with side effects to a macro. Use an inline function.

title: A 12 V input has a series Schottky diode for reverse-polarity protection. The load takes 1 A and the diode drops 0.4 V. How much power does the diode turn into heat?
explain: Power = voltage drop × current = 0.4 V × 1 A = 0.4 W. A diode is simple but always wastes this power, and the load gets less than 12 V. For high current, a P-channel MOSFET in the supply line has a drop of only millivolts and also blocks reverse polarity.

title: Cortex-M interrupt priorities: 5 rules
bullets: A lower number means a higher priority. Priority 0 is the strongest.
Chips implement only the top bits (4 on many STM32). Use the HAL macro, not a raw value like 3 in the register.
A higher-priority ISR can interrupt a lower one. Equal or lower ones wait (pending).
With FreeRTOS, ISRs that call FromISR functions must have a number at or above configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY.
Keep SysTick and PendSV at the lowest priority, so they never block device ISRs.
